title: Derive components from the feature's ioSeeds and WMBT verbs

facts.note: Lexical hint: task text mentions components, ioSeeds, WMBTs or features. Fires regardless of whether the feature currently has ioSeeds or WMBTs; with neither present, the rule still applies and forbids inventing components.
Whether the planner is generating, adding or re-deriving a feature's components (not merely editing prose) is judged from the task.
Needs a diff-level observer detecting component entries added/changed in planning artifacts, or ioSeeds/WMBT edits on a feature that already has components.
Planner phase is not currently emitted as an observable fact.

fires: Planner generates the component list for a feature that has ioSeeds, WMBTs, or both.
Planner generates components for a feature that has only WMBTs (no ioSeeds), or only ioSeeds (no WMBTs).
Planner is asked to generate or add components for a feature that has neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs: the rule fires and any component without a trigger is rejected as invented.
Planner adds a new component to an existing feature plan.
Planner revises a feature's WMBTs or ioSeeds and re-derives its existing components.
doesNotFire: Planner edits a feature's description or acceptance wording without touching components, ioSeeds or WMBTs.
Coder implements an already-planned component in code.
Planner authors wagon-level docs that list no components.

given: A feature's components are being planned, whatever ioSeeds (consume/produce) or WMBTs the feature currently has, including none
when: the planner generates, adds or re-derives that feature's components
then: Derive each component from a concrete ioSeed trigger or WMBT verb in the feature, with the business capability and layer the derivation map gives that trigger.
prefer: Steps: analyze ioSeeds/WMBTs → identify needed capabilities → assign layers → generate up to 8 components with complete structure → confirm all feature needs are covered.

ioSeeds map: produce event:*/notification:* → event publishing (application|integration); consume event:*/notification:* → event handling (application|integration); consume command:* → command processing (application); produce query:* → query handling (application|domain).

WMBT verbs map: validate/verify/check → validator (domain); process/compute/calculate → processor (application|domain); display/show/render → display (presentation); store/save/persist → persister (integration); coordinate/orchestrate/manage → coordinator (application).
Examples: WMBT 'persist choice' → ChoicePersister at integration; ioSeeds.consume has command:* → command-processing component at application.
Where the map allows two layers (a|b), either listed layer complies; the source gives no tie-breaker, so record which trigger justified the chosen layer.

If the feature has neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs, or covering every trigger would need more than 8 components, report that conflict instead of inventing components, exceeding the cap or silently dropping coverage.
avoid: Inventing a component with no ioSeed or WMBT trigger behind it.
More than 8 components for one feature.
Leaving an ioSeed trigger or WMBT need uncovered.
why: Deriving components from ioSeeds and WMBTs keeps generation systematic and traceable: every component exists because a concrete trigger in the feature called for it.
evidence: Each planned component can be traced to an ioSeed entry or WMBT verb of the feature.
Each component's business capability and layer match the derivation map entry for its trigger.
The feature has at most 8 components.
Every ioSeed trigger and WMBT need of the feature is covered by at least one component.
A feature with neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs has no derived components; any component listed for it is a finding.
verifier_detail: Derivation from ioSeeds (from_io_seeds): ioSeeds triggers generate components with event-publishing, event-handling, command-processing, or query-handling capability. produce_events: trigger feature.ioSeeds.produce contains event:* or notification:* → Component with event publishing capability, layer application or integration. consume_events: trigger feature.ioSeeds.consume contains event:* or notification:* → Component with event handling capability, layer application or integration. consume_commands: trigger feature.ioSeeds.consume contains command:* → Component with command processing capability, layer application. produce_queries: trigger feature.ioSeeds.produce contains query:* → Component with query handling capability, layer application or domain.

Derivation from WMBT analysis (from_wmbt_analysis): WMBT verbs generate validation, processing, presentation, persistence, or coordination components with a business capability and layer. validation_needs: WMBTs contain 'validate','verify','check' → Validation component, business_capability validator, layer domain. processing_needs: 'process','compute','calculate' → Processing component, processor, application or domain. presentation_needs: 'display','show','render' → Presentation component, display, presentation. persistence_needs: 'store','save','persist' → Persistence component, persister, integration. coordination_needs: 'coordinate','orchestrate','manage' → Coordination component, coordinator, application.

Component generation strategy (generation_strategy): the end-to-end strategy from feature analysis to validated components. step_1_analyze: analyze feature ioSeeds and WMBTs; step_2_identify: identify needed business capabilities; step_3_assign: assign capabilities to appropriate layers; step_4_generate: generate up to 8 components with complete structure; step_5_validate: ensure all feature needs covered by components.

Feature-to-component mapping example (mapping_example, binary_choice_feature): a binary-choice feature with consume/produce ioSeeds and WMBTs maps to validator, processor, and display components. Input ioSeeds.consume: [dilemma:presented]; ioSeeds.produce: [decision:made]; wmbts: [validate options, process choice, display result]. Output components: option-validator @ domain (reason: WMBT mentions validation); choice-processor @ application (reason: WMBT mentions processing); result-display @ presentation (reason: WMBT mentions display).

Examples: WMBT 'persist choice' → ChoicePersister at integration; feature.ioSeeds.consume contains command:* → command-processing component at application. Counter-example: inventing a component with no ioSeed or WMBT trigger behind it.
Applicability does not depend on ioSeeds/WMBTs being present: when both are absent, every component in the feature is untriggered and therefore a counter-example finding.

additions.text: Coverage (step 5) and the 8-component cap (step 4) are independent obligations; suggested as planner.component.coverage and planner.component.limit. Kept here as prefer/avoid since they are part of the same derivation decision.
Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire, including re-derivation when ioSeeds/WMBTs change and the no-trigger case (feature with neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs).
additions.justification: Source has no activation metadata; derived from statement scope and counter-example S012, which must be enforced precisely when no trigger exists.

additions.text: prefer[4]: where the map allows two layers, either complies; record the justifying trigger.
additions.justification: Source lists alternative layers without a selection criterion; this states that both are compliant (no new restriction) and asks only for traceability already implied by the summary (S009).

additions.text: prefer[5]: report rather than resolve silently when there is no trigger at all or when full coverage would exceed 8 components.
additions.justification: Source steps 4 and 5 and counter-example S012 can conflict; source offers no reconciliation, so the planner surfaces the conflict instead of breaking one of them.
